character: Wolf Heimlich and Detective O'Riley after Ziggy's murder
voice: Wolf is severe and coercive; O'Riley is patronizing and territorial without stage-Irish spelling or torture-parody shorthand.

entries.text: What is going on in here?
I'd say you have some explaining to do, young lady. Why were you screaming?
I... found... Mr. Ziggy's head.
You have an unfortunate habit of finding bodies, Miss Bow. We should return to my office and question you properly.
Easy, Wolf. The young lady has just found a man's head. Give her a moment before you begin your inquisition.
Thank you, Mr. O'Riley.
Don't thank me, Miss Bow. I'm not saying you didn't kill him. I'm merely keeping Heimlich from frightening the answers out of you.
I will get results. Let me question her alone.
I know you're eager to help, Wolf, but I can question the lady without your assistance.
And if she lies? You would never know. Your methods are too lenient.
I just walked in and found his head. That's all.
Heimlich has a point, Miss Bow. It's curious that you keep reaching murder scenes before anyone else. How do you account for that?
Just lucky, I guess.
You seem a bit small to saw through a man's neck. That is one point in your favor.
Thanks.
She could have had help. Or perhaps you underestimate her.
Or perhaps you're pinning the murders on her so you can catch a culprit and save your job.
My position is secure, Detective.
Is it, now? A security chief who lets thieves carry off the exhibits and overlooks several murders beneath his nose? I'd reconsider your methods if I were running this museum.
This is neither the time nor place to debate my methods. We have a suspect to question.
Correction: we have a murder scene to investigate. We can question Miss Bow after she's had time to recover.
Thank you again, sir.
You've got a strong stomach, I'll grant you. One scream and you've already got your head together again, so to speak. Don't try to leave the museum.
I can't leave. I'm locked in.
Good. One less problem to manage.
Come along, Wolf. We have work to do. Let's fetch the crime-scene tools.
